example.title: Philadelphia & Reading Railroad, Mill Creek Bridge

brief: Five-span segmental stone arch railway bridge on a slight curve, spans of 27 ft 9 in to 30 ft 4 in rising 7 ft (inner) to 11 ft (end arches), the three middle arches over the creek and the two end arches over local lanes, separated by wide pilasters. Rectangular cut stone: smooth-faced in the barrels, heavy rock-faced on piers, pilasters and spandrels, with projecting rock-faced voussoirs; cobbled creek bed under the arches. A 1917 concrete deck 24 ft wide with steel pipe railings replaced the coping, and utility pipes run along the fascia. For the 7 m Sauk Creek crossing use one arch of this family (about 28 ft, 7 ft rise) with a pilaster at each end.
